height_sensitive_topics: Classification as a high-rise / tall / higher-risk building and the extra approval gateway or independent peer review this triggers
Sprinkler protection and water supply: whether, standard, pump redundancy, tanks, standpipes/risers
Firefighting shaft or fire-fighting lift(s): number, size, power supply, lobby, shaft pressurisation
Number of stairs, whether a second stair is needed, stair width, scissor stair acceptability, refuge floors, evacuation lifts, travel distances
Stair and lobby smoke control: pressurisation, smoke extract, smoke-control design standard
Structural fire resistance period and compartmentation (floor/wall ratings, protection of the structural frame, concrete spalling)
Façade and cladding fire performance: reaction-to-fire classes, cavity barriers, limits on combustible materials, external fire spread tests
Fire command centre, emergency voice communication, firefighter access, aerial appliance reach limits, dry/wet risers, fire-service communications
Emergency and standby power, duration, fire-rated cabling
Wind: need for wind-tunnel testing or high-frequency force balance, serviceability accelerations, façade pressures, dynamic response, tornado/cyclone provisions
Seismic: importance factor / risk category / consequence class, height limits for structural systems, irregularity limits, nonlinear time-history or peer review, drift limits, detailing class
Structural robustness / disproportionate collapse and progressive collapse requirements
Foundation and basement: geotechnical category, deep excavation, groundwater, liquefaction, independent geotechnical review
Design life, durability class and exposure, special inspection or independent supervision regime
Lifts: evacuation lifts, number and speed, lift lobby protection, access for stretcher
Accessibility: accessible apartments proportion, accessible refuge, lift sizes (cross-check with bld-accessibility)
Energy and overheating at height: envelope performance, glazing ratio, solar, ventilation, thermal comfort
Planning: aviation obstacle limits, overshadowing, wind microclimate assessment at pedestrian level, heritage view corridors
Fire engineering: whether performance-based (alternative solution) design is mandatory above some height and the peer-review process
Rooftop plant, helipad / aircraft warning lights, lightning protection, window cleaning / BMU anchorage, and construction-stage fire safety

tall_building_requirements.statement: AS/NZS 1170.2:2021 per a search summary: dynamic analysis required where first-mode frequency below 0.2 Hz, height above 200 m, or significant modal coupling; structures outside scope need specialist techniques including wind-tunnel testing; roofs/podiums at the base of tall buildings may need wind-tunnel advice. Tower is about 94 m plus 5 m plant, so below the 200 m scope limit quoted; T1 from structure/seismic returns (about 4.55 s, f about 0.22 Hz) is close to the 0.2 Hz trigger, so the trigger must be checked with real stiffness.
tall_building_requirements.status: verify clause numbers; a mandatory wind-tunnel rule for towers of this height was NOT found

tall_building_requirements.statement: NCC performance-based design: Performance Solutions are an alternative to DTS; need for independent peer review is decided at the Performance-Based Design Brief stage (search summary). Buildings above 25 m effective height require major fire safety systems; Spec 18 concessions do not apply.
